title: Chinese Braised Beef
subtitle: Slow-braised beef with soy, star anise, and five spice
excerpt: Chinese braised beef is a long, slow cook that fills the kitchen with the warm scent of star anise and five spice. Beef chuck is browned, then braised in soy, rice wine, and stock until pull-apart tender. The braising liquid is reduced to a sauce and poured over sliced beef. Simple and deeply flavoured.
sourceNotes: Slow-braised beef with soy sauce, star anise, and five spice is a staple of Shanghainese and Cantonese home cooking. The dish is often made with a whole piece of beef brisket or chuck, braised until pull-apart tender. It is served sliced with the braising liquid reduced to a glaze.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the beef in the reduced sauce. Defrost overnight and reheat gently on the hob.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: This dish improves the next day. Make ahead and reheat gently.

content.text: Good browning is the foundation of this dish. Take the time to colour the beef well on all sides before the liquid goes in -- it adds depth that the braise alone cannot provide. After that, low and slow is the method. The beef needs a very gentle simmer for the collagen to break down properly.

items.prepNote: cut into large chunks or left whole
use Shaoxing rice wine or dry sherry

content.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large saucepan over high heat. Brown the beef on all sides -- about 8 minutes total. Remove and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add the ginger, garlic, star anise, and five spice. Fry for 1 minute.
Add the brown sugar and stir until it melts. Pour in the rice wine, then the soy sauce and stock.
Return the beef to the pan. The liquid should come about halfway up the beef. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a very low simmer.
Cover and braise for 90 minutes, turning the beef every 30 minutes, until very tender.
Remove the beef. Increase the heat and reduce the braising liquid for 10 minutes to a sauce consistency. Pour over the sliced beef.

items.cause: Braised at too high a temperature or wrong cut
items.fix: Beef chuck needs a long, very slow braise. Make sure the liquid is barely simmering -- not boiling. If still tough, cover and continue for another 30 minutes. The collagen needs time to break down.

content.text: Braised beef with soy and star anise is a dish found in Chinese homes across the country. It is slow cooking at its most fragrant. The star anise and five spice give it a distinctive warmth. Serve sliced with the reduced braising sauce and plain white rice.
